# Ontology Product foundation implementation

- Plan: `CAL-MIGRATION-0004-ONTOLOGY-PRODUCT-FOUNDATION-IMPLEMENTATION-V1`
- Unit: `CML11-S2-SOURCE-PRESERVING-ONTOLOGY-FOUNDATION`
- Status: `implementation-directed-candidate`
- Authority effect: `none`

## Objective

Implement one source-preserving Ontology Product foundation that keeps the migrated CyberAlchemy-v2 business ontology distinct from the Product scaffold and registers the governed ontology-package output as a four-facet Artifact Type candidate.

## Product construction

- A byte-preserving import of the six CyberAlchemy-v2 Product Ontology registries
- A separate successor source-binding ledger that exposes rather than overwrites legacy digest drift
- An Ontology Package/v1 Artifact Type candidate with closed schema, generated human projection, hostile fixtures, and validation receipt
- A successor construction candidate bound to the predecessor and new evidence

## Done criteria

- All six imported registries are byte-identical to their selected sources
- All eight legacy source bindings resolve through explicit current successor bindings and exactly three declared drift reconciliations
- The imported ontology retains 23 nodes, 24 relations, 13 relation types, and 5 residue records
- The imported business ontology remains distinct from the three-node Product Ontology scaffold and from the Product output
- Ontology Package/v1 validates the current Product package witness and rejects authority inflation, missing source binding, and unknown fields
- Every human view is a deterministic generated projection
- The successor candidate and all receipts preserve authority_effect none
